newsitem.title: USA: Clinton announces deal on balanced-budget plan.
newsitem.headline: Clinton announces deal on balanced-budget plan.

text.p: President Bill Clinton announced on Friday he has reached accord with congressional Republican leaders on a plan to balance the U.S. federal budget by 2002.

"We have reached agreement in broad but fairly specific terms ... with Republican leaders today that would balance the budget by 2002," Clinton announced during a political trip to Baltimore. "It would be the first balanced budget in three decades."

Congressional sources in Washington said the deal would include a net tax cut of about $85 billion over five years -- a key to Republican support -- plus $600 to $700 billion in savings in entitlement programs over 10 years. It would slow the growth of spending on Medicare, the health program for the elderly, by $115 billion over five years.

Although it was expected the budget deal -- which must be approved by Congress -- would encounter opposition from both liberal Democrats and conservative Republicans, leaders of both parties joined Clinton in praising the pact on Friday.

"I think I can say with some confidence that the senators and congressmen standing behind me are indication of the degree of support there is in our Democratic caucus," said Senate Democratic Leader Tom Daschle, who had joined Clinton for a party leadership meeting in Baltimore. "And I am confident today that a majority of Democrats in the U.S. Senate will support this agreement."
In Washington, the leading Republican negotiator, Sen. Pete Domenici of New Mexico, said he was "very happy" with the agreement.
